units.zh: 后妃之制，厥有等威，其來尚矣。
units.en: The ranks and authority governing empresses and consorts are ancient institutions.
units.literal: The institution of empresses and consorts has its ranks and authority; its origin is of long standing.

units.zh: 元初，因其國俗，不娶庶姓，非此族也，不居嫡選。
units.en: Early in the dynasty the Mongols followed their own custom of not marrying outside certain clans; only women of the designated lineage could be chosen as principal consorts.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Yuan, following their national custom, they did not marry common clans; those not of this clan could not hold the principal selection.

units.zh: 當時史臣以為舅甥之貴，蓋有周姬、齊姜之遺意，歷世守之，固可嘉也。
units.en: Contemporary historians held that the esteem accorded maternal-kin marriage preserved something of the Zhou custom of taking brides from the Ji of Zhou and the Jiang of Qi—a practice maintained for generations and rightly praised.
units.literal: The historians of that time regarded the honor of uncle and nephew [alliances] as preserving something of the Zhou practice of Ji brides and Qi Jiang brides; to preserve this through generations was indeed commendable.

units.zh: 然其居則有曰斡耳朵之分，沒復有繼承守宮之法。
units.en: Yet their households were divided into separate ordas, and after a consort's death there arose the practice of heirs inheriting and maintaining her palace establishment.
units.literal: Yet in residence there were divisions called orda; after death there was again the method of inheriting and guarding the palace.

units.zh: 位號之淆，名分之瀆，則亦甚矣。
units.en: The confusion of titles and the breach of proper status were extreme as well.
units.literal: The confusion of titles and ranks, the violation of name and status, was indeed extreme.

units.zh: 累朝嘗詔有司修后妃傳，而未見成書。
units.en: Dynasty after dynasty the court ordered officials to compile biographies of empresses and consorts, yet no finished book ever appeared.
units.literal: Over successive reigns they often ordered the relevant offices to compile biographies of empresses and consorts, but no completed work is seen.

units.zh: 內廷事祕，今莫之考，則其氏名之僅見簡牘者，尚可遺而不錄乎？
units.en: Inner-palace affairs are secret and cannot now be fully verified; yet the clan names that survive on scattered documents surely ought not to be omitted.
units.literal: Inner-palace affairs are secret; none can examine them today—can the clan names that appear only on scattered documents still be left unrecorded?

units.zh: 且一代之制存焉，闕疑而慎言，斯可矣。
units.en: What remains here still preserves the institutions of an age; to note uncertainties and speak with caution is enough.
units.literal: Moreover, the institutions of a dynasty are preserved here; to leave doubts unspoken and speak cautiously is sufficient.

units.zh: 作后妃表。
units.en: Hence this table of empresses and consorts.
units.literal: [I therefore] compose the Table of Empresses and Consorts.

Right Great Orda: Empress Hulan; Empress Ha'erbazhen; Empress Yiqiliezhen; Empress Tuohucha'er; Consorts Yezhen, Yelihutu, Chazhen, and Halazhen. Second Empress Anghui. Third Empress Qilijihutieni. Sixth Empress Tunajina. Consort Yeliqina, mother of Mieli.
units.literal: Principal-palace Empress Boluhezhen. Sixth Empress Toregene (Naimazhen clan; in the year renyin Taizong died; the empress regent ruled the state for four years in all. In the second year of Zhiyuan posthumously titled Empress Zhaoci). Second Empress Anghui. Third Empress Qilijihutieni. Sixth Empress Tunajina. Consort Yeliqina (mother of Mieli).

units.zh: 斡兀立海迷失三皇后 （至元二年追諡欽淑皇后。）

units.zh: 火里差皇后 （火魯剌部人。） 忽都台皇后 （弘吉剌氏，按陳從孫女，至元二年追諡貞節皇后。） 也速兒皇后 （貞節妹也。） 出卑三皇后 （歲己未，從憲宗南伐，七月憲宗崩，九月八日后亦薨于六盤。） 明里忽都魯皇后 （泰定三年詔守班禿營帳。）
units.en: Empress Huolicha (of the Huolula tribe). Empress Hudutai (Kongirat, a collateral granddaughter of Anchannayan; posthumously titled Empress Zhenjie in 1265). Empress Yesu'er (Zhenjie's younger sister). units.literal: Great Empress Tegulün. units.en: Empress Buluhan (Baiyuewu, granddaughter of the meritorious minister Puhua and daughter of the imperial son-in-law Telihusi; made empress at the start of Yuanzhen and invested in 1299; when Temür died in 1307 Külüg deposed her, exiled her to Dong'an, and soon had her executed. Though she dominated the inner court during Temür's late illnesses, she trusted the chief minister Harqasun and helped bring the Dade reign to a stable close—a point critics still acknowledged). Primary Consort Shilian Dali (Kongirat; died young; posthumously titled Empress Zhenci Jingyi in 1308 and enshrined at Chengzong's temple). Empress Qilijihutieni.
units.literal: Empress Buluhan (Baiyuewu clan, granddaughter of meritorious minister Puhua, daughter of consort Telihusi; established as empress at the beginning of Yuanzhen; in the third year of Dade invested with seal and treasure; in the eleventh year the emperor died, Wuzong was established, the empress was deposed, moved to Dong'an Prefecture, and soon ordered to die by grant. In Chengzong's later years he had many illnesses; the empress held power within the palace yet was able to trust chief minister Harqasun, thereby completing the governance of Dade—those of discernment still found something to approve). units.en: Consort Daji (Kongirat; honored as Empress Dowager in 1307; in 1315 given the lengthy honorific Empress Dowager Yitian Xingsheng Ciren Zhaoyi Shouyuan Quande Taining Fuqing; raised to Grand Empress Dowager in 1320 with the added epithet Weiwen Chongyou; died in 1322 and was posthumously titled Empress Zhaoxian Yuansheng). She was clever but unrestrained; once established in the Eastern Palace her excesses deepened. Within the palace the "Black Donkey Mother" Yilieshiba dominated affairs; outside, favorites such as Shiliemen and Niulin, together with chief minister Tiemudier, abused imperial favor and corrupted government. After Gegeen acceded, this whole clique was executed and her influence waned.
units.literal: Consort Daji (Kongirat clan; in the eleventh year of Dade honored as Empress Dowager; in the second year of Yanyou elevated with honorific title Empress Dowager Yitian Xingsheng Ciren Zhaoyi Shouyuan Quande Taining Fuqing; in the seventh year again honored as Grand Empress Dowager, with added honorific Weiwen Chongyou; died in the third year of Zhizhi, posthumous title Empress Zhaoxian Yuansheng. The consort was intelligent, yet did not restrain herself; when she took the eastern court as her proper position, licentious indulgence grew worse; within, the Black Donkey Mother Yilieshiba held power; without, favored ministers Shiliemen, Niulin, and others together with the chief minister at the time Tiemudier relied on favor to do wrong and muddied court government. When Yingzong was established, the whole group of favorites was executed, and thereafter her blaze of power slightly subsided).

candidatePacket.instructions: Review dates, event ownership, conversions, endpoint evidence, age reckoning, omitted life dates, and active-date hints. Read all Chinese units for omissions; English is not independent evidence. Do not re-extract names or mentions. For each item identify whose event is dated and justify each endpoint. Same mother does not imply same birth year. Later allusions are not personal activity. Research or record a blocker rather than invent precision. A report cannot approve with missing checks or unresolved research.

findings.problem: A ruler-name table heading identifies the table column, but its Chinese text supplies no start or end year for the listed person. The extraction converts those headings into complete Western-life intervals.
findings.action: Replace each full reign-derived life interval with only a source-specific table association or an explicitly unresolved chronology; add an endpoint only after independently pinned source research.

findings.problem: These particular Chinese entries explicitly date a posthumous honor, enshrinement, or named reference to such an honor. Their later ceremony dates are encoded as ordinary personal attestations, which risks treating a deceased subject as active.
findings.action: Classify each dated ceremony or reference as a posthumous reception event for the honoree or referenced subject; retain the ceremony date and remove any active-date inference that rests only on that reception.

findings.problem: Several entries turn a broad reign phrase, another person’s dated honor, or an undated exile death into a point or closed activity interval. In particular, 卒徙所 follows the AD 1340 exile notice but does not say that death occurred in that year.
findings.action: Use the source wording and, where supported, a one-sided bound; otherwise retain a research hold. Do not borrow a relative’s, honoree’s, or officeholder’s date as the named person’s activity span.

findings.problem: The listed active-date hints either repeat an unsupported reign-table interval, borrow a related person’s dated act, or derive a living date from a posthumous reference. The chapter does not supply an independent life endpoint for them.
findings.action: Remove the unsupported active hint or replace it with a source-specific unresolved research hold. Keep a later reception visible separately rather than converting it into a life date.
